function: no_learning: only a DNN fitting the RIS element response is learned (p. 5, p. 6); channel estimation is least squares (p. 8), beamforming is Adam optimization (p. 10).
notes: PDF is arXiv v1 (2510.20354, 23 Oct 2025), titled Channel Estimation and Passive Beamforming for Pixel-based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces with Non-Separable State Response; it does not print the DOI. Borderline case. The only trained model is a DNN fitted by regression (NMSE loss, p. 6) to the response of one RIS element, which p. 4 says "is determined solely by the structure of the pixel RIS element", so it does not depend on the propagation channel. Channel estimation is least squares over dominant rays (p. 8, Algorithms 1 and 2) and passive beamforming is a continuous relaxation solved per realization with Adam (p. 10); no network is trained for the estimation or the beamforming step, and all rate baselines are non-learned: Random, Best Sounding, Group-Opt, Phased Array (p. 11). If the reviewer counts the DNN surrogate as a learned physical-layer component, the closest area is 3 and the marks would be q1=1 (p. 10: 3GPP ray-tracing model of TS 38.901, Indoor-Office), q2=0, q3=0, q4=1 (Table II, p. 7: FLOPs and parameters), q5=0 (no code or data link).
